title: Big Kato and Little Kato, pianists
summary: Vincent describes the two Katos as piano players, one a chord player who could barely read, the other a reader, and discusses their disabilities.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Ask him about Big and Little Kato.

He said, what about Big Kato and Little Kato? Oh, well, Little Kato. You know him, huh? You know what I'm talking about? He was a piano player. Both of them piano. But Little Kato, he was a musician. He could have been there. And that's when I told him to play all those ninth cards and six cards, you know, like that, and the minister cards, when they take a hat. We couldn't play behind him, you know what he'd be making. And after he kept on doing it, we had to tell him, you know, we couldn't play, but he had to play by himself, you know. And he asked him, hi, Simon. He said, it sounds rotten. He said, the justice is kicking about it now. And I said, I don't like it, you know. But he stopped, you know. Everything in him was a mind card player. Everything in mind, you know, took a hat, you know. But he was a good piano player. But I think he could just read just a little bit, not much. That's Big Kato. Little Kato, he could read. Tall, he was such a fellow.
Big Kato was blind. I know.
You said Big Kato was blind, eh? Well, he was blind lately.
No, I mean he couldn't read. He couldn't read.

You mean he couldn't read music. Oh, no. He meant he could read a little bit, not much, you see. Then he had a, I believe he was, I believe he was blind and a kid and had one leg and play bass. Then the young one, his daddy, could play drum, you see. And there wasn't one leg to play drum too, you know, drum and bass.
